title: K-wise independence fools low-degree polynomials
statement: Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, and let $\mu$ be a probability distribution on $\{0,1\}^n$ such that every set of at most $k$ coordinates has a uniform joint distribution. If $P$ is a multilinear polynomial in the coordinate indicators, of degree at most $k$, evaluated on the Boolean cube, then its expectation under $\mu$ equals its expectation under the uniform distribution on $\{0,1\}^n$.
hypotheses_covered: Probability distribution mu on the n-dimensional Boolean cube
Every coordinate set of size at most k has uniform joint distribution under mu
P has a multilinear monomial expansion on the Boolean cube
Coefficients of monomials of degree greater than k vanish
